skill.name: frontend-accessibility
skill.description: Build accessible frontend interfaces with semantic HTML, ARIA, keyboard support, focus management, labels, contrast checks, and screen reader guidance.
skill.summary: Guide frontend code toward semantic, keyboard-friendly, screen reader compatible interfaces.
skill.author: EIS-ITS

content.value_statement: Inaccessible interfaces exclude users and create compliance risk. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to build WCAG-aligned frontend experiences.
actual_capabilities: Guides semantic HTML choices for templates and component markup.
Recommends ARIA attributes for interactive elements when native HTML is not enough.
Supports keyboard navigation and focus management for menus, modals, and overlays.
Improves forms with labels, validation messages, and accessible field relationships.
Checks heading structure, image text alternatives, color contrast, and screen reader support.
limitations: Does not run automated accessibility scanners by itself.
Does not guarantee legal compliance without human review.
Depends on project code and design context supplied by the user.
May need manual testing with assistive technology for final validation.

use_cases.title: Create Accessible Components
use_cases.description: Build buttons, forms, navigation, and dialogs with semantic markup and keyboard support.

use_cases.title: Review Product Flows
use_cases.description: Check key user flows for labels, focus order, headings, contrast, and screen reader clarity.

use_cases.title: Refactor Legacy Interfaces
use_cases.description: Identify accessibility gaps in existing UI code and prioritize practical improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Check A Simple Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small UI element.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component for accessibility. Focus on semantic HTML, labels, keyboard behavior, and screen reader output.

prompt_templates.title: Improve A Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this form plan for accessibility. Include labels, required fields, error messages, help text, and focus handling.

prompt_templates.title: Audit An Interactive Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of menus, dialogs, or overlays.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this interactive flow for keyboard navigation, focus management, ARIA usage, escape behavior, and readable state changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A WCAG Refactor
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced accessibility remediation across a frontend area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a prioritized accessibility refactor plan for this frontend area. Cover semantic structure, contrast, forms, media, testing, and release risks.

output_examples.input: A checkout form needs an accessibility review.
output_examples.output: A prioritized list covering missing labels, unclear error messages, focus order, required field cues, and screen reader announcements.

output_examples.input: A modal dialog is being added to a React page.
output_examples.output: Guidance for focus trapping, initial focus, escape behavior, close controls, background content handling, and dialog naming.

output_examples.input: A navigation menu must work for keyboard users.
output_examples.output: Recommendations for semantic structure, tab order, visible focus, expanded state, menu activation, and mobile behavior.

best_practices: Start with native HTML elements before adding ARIA roles or custom behavior.
Test keyboard paths, focus visibility, labels, and error states during development.
Validate important flows with automated checks and manual screen reader testing.
anti_patterns: Replacing native controls with custom elements that lack keyboard support.
Using ARIA attributes to mask incorrect semantics or missing labels.
Relying only on color, icons, or visual position to communicate meaning.

faq.question: Does this skill replace accessibility testing tools?
faq.answer: No. It guides implementation choices, but automated scans and manual assistive technology tests are still needed.

faq.question: Can it help with React and Vue components?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill applies to component markup, forms, dialogs, navigation, and dynamic views.

faq.question: Does it cover WCAG requirements?
faq.answer: It supports WCAG-oriented practices such as contrast, labels, headings, keyboard access, and screen reader compatibility.

faq.question: Will it make every interface fully compliant?
faq.answer: No. Compliance depends on complete product context, implementation quality, content, and validation by qualified reviewers.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when creating, reviewing, or refactoring frontend UI that people must navigate, read, or operate.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Provide the component, user flow, design intent, expected interactions, validation rules, and any accessibility concerns.
